_meta.name: RegRadar default customer risk model
_meta.status: DEFAULT, configure for your firm. The factor list follows the EBA risk-factor categories; weights, option scores, thresholds and review periods are a starting judgement, not a regulatory requirement.
_meta.scale: Each answer carries a score from 1 (lowest risk) to 5 (highest). The customer score is the weighted average of the answers, rescaled to 0 (all answers score 1) to 100 (all answers score 5).

sources.label: EBA Guidelines EBA/GL/2021/02 on customer due diligence and the ML/TF risk factors, as amended by EBA/GL/2024/01 (16 January 2024)
sources.used_for: Guideline 2 (identifying risk factors: customer, countries and geographical areas, products/services/transactions, delivery channels), Guideline 3.2 (holistic view of all factors), Guideline 4 (CDD measures), Guideline 21 (crypto-asset service providers: 21.3 product, 21.5 customer and behaviour, 21.7 geography, 21.9 channel, 21.12 enhanced CDD).

sources.label: Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 (AMLR), Chapter III Customer due diligence
sources.used_for: Arts 19-26 (CDD), 29 (high-risk third countries), 33 (simplified), 34 (enhanced), 40 (self-hosted addresses), 41 (residence by investment), 42, 45, 46 (PEPs), 69 and 73 (reporting, no disclosure).

sources.label: RegRadar Country risk data (data/country-risk.json)
sources.used_for: Country composite score, tier and listings (FATF, EU high-risk third countries, EU non-cooperative tax list, sanctions exposure).

geo.note: Mirrors the Balanced preset of the Country risk page: composite 0 to 10 from the weighted indicators, Low below 3.5, High from 6.5. Edit to match your own country policy.

groups.label: Customer type and ownership
groups.eba: EBA GL 2 (customer risk factors); GL 21.5(a) for crypto customers

groups.label: Geography
groups.eba: EBA GL 2 (countries and geographical areas); GL 21.7 for crypto

groups.label: Products, services and channels
groups.eba: EBA GL 2 (products, services, transactions and delivery channels); GL 21.3 and 21.9 for crypto

groups.label: Expected activity and behaviour
groups.eba: EBA GL 2 and GL 4 (understanding purpose, source of funds, ongoing monitoring); GL 21.5(b) for crypto behaviour

groups.label: PEP, sanctions and adverse media
groups.eba: EBA GL 2 and GL 4; AMLR Arts 20(1)(d), 20(1)(g), 41, 42, 45, 46

factors.label: Customer type
factors.help: Legal form and whether the customer is regulated, listed or a more opaque vehicle.

options.label: Natural person, resident in the EEA
Natural person, resident outside the EEA
Regulated EU credit or financial institution
Company listed on a regulated market, or public body
Private company or sole trader, local operations
Private company with foreign incorporation or operations
Non-profit organisation or charity
Holding, investment vehicle or special-purpose vehicle
Trust, foundation or similar legal arrangement

factors.label: Sector of activity
factors.help: EBA GL 2.4(b) lists certain money service businesses, crypto-asset service providers, casinos and dealers in precious metals as sectors associated with higher risk.

options.label: Ordinary commercial activity or salaried / pension income
Cash-intensive business (retail, hospitality, vending)
High-value goods, real estate, art or precious metals
Money service business or payment intermediary
Crypto-asset service provider or crypto-related business
Gambling or casino
Arms, defence or dual-use goods
Business activity unclear or not evidenced

factors.label: Ownership structure and complexity
factors.help: Number of layers between the customer and the natural persons who ultimately own or control it, and whether nominees or bearer shares are used.

options.label: Not applicable (natural person)
Simple: owners hold shares directly, one layer
Two to three layers, all in transparent jurisdictions
Four or more layers, cross-border chain, or a trust in the chain
Opaque: nominee shareholders or directors, bearer shares, or no clear commercial reason for the structure

factors.label: Identification and verification status
factors.help: How far CDD is complete for the customer and its beneficial owners (AMLR Arts 20-23).

options.label: Customer and beneficial owners identified and verified
Verified in part: senior managing official used as the fallback (Art. 22(2))
Documents or verification still outstanding
CDD cannot be completed (refused, unverifiable or inconsistent)

factors.label: Relationship and entity history
factors.help: EBA GL 21.5(a)(iii) names a recently established company processing large volumes as an increasing factor.

options.label: Established customer, or entity with a longstanding record
New entity (under 12 months) or no prior history
Recently established company expected to process large volumes

factors.label: Country of residence or incorporation
factors.help: Tier from the Country risk data, with the FATF, EU and sanctions listings shown beside it.

factors.label: Beneficial owner or controller: nationality and residence (highest-risk country)
factors.help: Pick the highest-risk country among the beneficial owners and controllers.

factors.label: Main counterparty or transfer corridor (highest-risk country)
factors.help: Pick the highest-risk country the customer expects to send money to or receive money from.

factors.label: Product or service
factors.help: The product the customer will use. Low limits and limited functionality reduce risk; anonymity and cross-border reach increase it (EBA GL 21.3, 21.4).

options.label: Limited-function product (closed loop, low limits)
Payment account or e-money wallet, EEA transfers
Reloadable card or prepaid card
Merchant acquiring or payment initiation for merchants
Cross-border payments or remittance outside the EEA
Crypto exchange (fiat to crypto) or custodial wallet
Crypto transfers, including to or from self-hosted addresses

factors.label: Onboarding channel
factors.help: EBA GL 21.9(a): remote onboarding that does not comply with the EBA Guidelines on remote customer onboarding (EBA/GL/2022/15) is an increasing factor.

options.label: Face to face
Remote, using a solution that follows EBA/GL/2022/15
Introduced by an intermediary (reliance on a third party)
Remote, solution not aligned with EBA/GL/2022/15 or not verified
Introduced by an intermediary that is unregulated or in a high-risk jurisdiction

factors.label: Funding and payment instruments
factors.help: EBA GL 21.3(b): third-party payments with no apparent rationale increase risk; no restriction on cash or exempt e-money is a channel risk (GL 21.9(b)).

options.label: Own account at an EEA credit institution
Own account plus occasional third-party payers with a clear rationale
Third-party payments allowed or used without clear rationale
Cash, or anonymous or exempt e-money

factors.label: Expected monthly volume (EUR)
factors.help: Default bands are illustrative. Set them against your own business model and monitoring scenarios.

options.label: Under 2,000

factors.label: Purpose and economic rationale (Art. 25)
factors.help: Can the customer explain why they want the relationship and does it fit their profile?

options.label: Clear and consistent with the customer's profile
Plausible but not evidenced
Unclear, vague or inconsistent with the profile

factors.label: Source of funds and wealth
factors.help: AMLR Art. 25(c) and Art. 34(4)(c).

options.label: Documented and consistent
Plausible, partly evidenced
Unexplained or not evidenced
None
A minority of transfers
Most transfers

factors.label: Behaviour against the stated profile
factors.help: At onboarding use the stated profile and any pre-contact signals; at review use observed behaviour. EBA GL 4.60 and GL 21.5(b): transactions that differ in amount, frequency or complexity from what is expected.

options.label: Consistent with the profile
Minor deviations, explained
Unexplained deviations, structuring signs or rapid in-and-out movement

factors.label: Crypto: self-hosted, DeFi and privacy exposure
factors.help: EBA GL 21.3(d) and 21.5(b): self-hosted addresses, decentralised platforms, mixers and anonymity-enhancing tools. Choose 'Not applicable' for customers without crypto services.

options.label: Not applicable (no crypto-asset services)
Transfers only to or from wallets at regulated providers
Some self-hosted transfers, ownership confirmed
Significant self-hosted or DeFi use, ownership unconfirmed
Mixers, privacy-enhancing tools or darknet exposure

factors.label: PEP status (customer or beneficial owner)
factors.help: AMLR Art. 20(1)(g) requires the determination; Arts 42, 45 and 46 set the measures for PEPs, former PEPs, family members and close associates.

options.label: Not a PEP, family member or close associate
Former PEP, left office more than 12 months ago (residual risk assessed)
Former PEP, left office within the last 12 months
Politically exposed person
Family member of a PEP
Known close associate of a PEP

factors.label: Targeted financial sanctions screening
factors.help: AMLR Art. 20(1)(d): screen the customer and beneficial owners, including persons holding more than 50% or a majority interest.

options.label: No match
Potential match under review
Confirmed match (customer, beneficial owner or controller)
No adverse media found
Unconfirmed, minor or old reports
Credible reports of financial crime, corruption or terrorism links

factors.label: Prior suspicion on file (restricted)
factors.help: Restricted information. AMLR Art. 73(1) prohibits disclosing to the customer or third persons that a transaction is or has been assessed under Art. 69. Limit who can see this answer.

options.label: None
A report or internal suspicion exists for this customer

factors.label: Residence-by-investment applicant
factors.help: AMLR Art. 41: third-country nationals applying for residence rights in exchange for an investment.

options.label: No
Yes

rules.label: Confirmed targeted financial sanctions match
rules.basis: AMLR Art. 20(1)(d) and Art. 21(1): CDD includes the sanctions check; if CDD cannot be completed the firm refrains from the relationship. Escalate to your sanctions procedure.

rules.label: CDD cannot be completed
rules.basis: AMLR Art. 21(1): refrain from the transaction or relationship, terminate it and consider a report to the FIU.

rules.label: A linked country is on the FATF black list
rules.basis: Firm policy default (same as the Country risk page). Many firms decline or escalate every such case; configure to your risk appetite.

rules.label: A linked country has sanctions exposure of 9 or more (analyst-assigned, 0 to 10)
rules.basis: Firm policy default (same as the Country risk page, Balanced preset). The 0 to 10 sanctions score is subjective in the source data.

rules.label: A linked country is on the EU list of high-risk third countries
rules.basis: AMLR Art. 29(4): enhanced due diligence measures listed in Art. 34(4) apply to relationships involving persons from the country. Check the Commission's delegated act for country-specific measures.

rules.label: PEP, former PEP (12 months), family member or close associate
rules.basis: AMLR Arts 42, 45 and 46: senior management approval, source of wealth and funds, enhanced ongoing monitoring.

rules.label: Residence-by-investment applicant
rules.basis: AMLR Art. 41: at least the Art. 34(4) measures (a), (c), (e) and (f).

rules.label: Potential sanctions match not yet resolved
rules.basis: Firm policy default: treat as High until the alert is cleared. Do not onboard with an open potential match.

rules.label: Credible adverse media on financial crime
Prior suspicion on file
rules.basis: Firm policy default. Restricted: see AMLR Art. 73(1).

rules.label: Opaque ownership: nominees, bearer shares or unexplained structure
rules.basis: Firm policy default, based on EBA GL 2 customer risk factors and AMLR Art. 34(2) scrutiny of complex structures.

rules.label: Mixer, privacy tool or darknet exposure (crypto)
rules.basis: Firm policy default, based on EBA GL 21.3(d)(iv) and 21.5(b).

rules.label: A linked country is on the FATF grey list
rules.basis: Firm policy default: at least Medium. The score already weights the listing.

rules.label: A linked country is on the EU list of non-cooperative tax jurisdictions
